keywords: why do car rear windows have lines

scenes.visual: illustration of the back of a small hatchback car parked on a quiet Indian street in the early morning, seen straight from behind, the rear window glass shows thin horizontal orange-brown lines running across it, the car in the lower two-thirds of the frame
scenes.narration: You've seen these thin lines on the back window of a car, right? Ever wondered what they're *doing* there?

scenes.visual: illustration of a young Indian man standing behind a parked car, scratching his head with a puzzled smile, looking at the thin lines on the car's rear window, side view
scenes.narration: Most of us think they're just a design thing. Honestly, I thought that too. <chuckles> Nope.
scenes.headline: JUST *DESIGN*?

scenes.visual: 2D animation: the rear glass with thin lines; a dashboard button is pressed and current runs along every line
scenes.narration: Each line is a very thin strip of *metal*. Press a little button on the dashboard, and electricity runs through all of them.
scenes.headline: THIN *METAL* LINES

scenes.visual: illustration of a cosy kitchen toaster with its thin heating coils glowing warm orange inside, two slices of bread above it, simple kitchen counter
scenes.narration: Here's the thing. Push electricity through a thin wire, and it pushes back a little... so the wire *warms up*. Same idea as a toaster, just much gentler.
scenes.headline: LIKE A *TOASTER*

scenes.visual: 2D animation: the fogged rear glass clears outward from each warm line while a counter drops from 100% to 0%
scenes.narration: That gentle heat goes straight into the glass. So the *fog* just fades away, line by line... and on cold mornings, even the frost melts.
scenes.headline: FOG *GONE*

scenes.visual: illustration of the view through a perfectly clear car rear window from the back seat, a sunny Indian street visible behind the car, thin orange lines across the glass
scenes.narration: Your front windscreen clears fog with warm air from the vents. <short pause> The back window? It gets its own heater, built right into the glass.
scenes.headline: A HEATER IN THE *GLASS*

scenes.visual: 2D animation: a phone shares this video to a friend who replies
scenes.narration: So next foggy morning, press that button and watch the glass clear. That's your little 'oh, that's why' moment, right there.
scenes.headline: TRY IT *TOMORROW*
